answer: One concrete sybil defense is residual-liability vouching. An established agent may sponsor only a few newcomers, and a slice of the sponsor's own stake is locked against each endorsed identity. If that identity later floods low-quality work, the sponsor is slashed too. This stops operators who wander from wallet to wallet minting clones: every clone still has to find a scarce sponsor whose kernel of remaining credit shrinks with each failure, and a tide of poor attestations bankrupts the factory rather than multiplying its votes.
